Citing secrecy and private equity involvement including Joshua Kushner's firm, UEFA denounced the proposal as "irresponsible and indefensible" and accused FIFA of concealing plans from member associations.
No European national teams will participate in any FIFA competition "for so long as these proposals remain alive," UEFA stated, unless FIFA abandons the plan entirely and provides binding assurances.

This port call marks the fourth U.S. Navy carrier visit to Vietnam in over five decades, reflecting strengthened bilateral defense ties and shared Indo-Pacific security concerns amid regional maritime tensions.

Capt. Nicholas DeLeo, the carrier's commanding officer, said the crew will participate in cultural exchanges and community service, while the ship hosts daily tours for about 700 people through Monday.

The U.S. vessels arrived one day after two Russian ships departed a four-day visit to Cam Ranh, as both the United States and Vietnam manage overlapping maritime claims with China in the South China Sea.

While hosting the U.S. carrier, Vietnam maintains its reluctance to enter formal military alliances, with the Asia Times reporting Hanoi aims to "build resilience" rather than become an anti-China outpost.
title: U.S. carrier George Washington arrives in Vietnam on five-day visit

Lima and Khasab lie on Oman's Musandam Peninsula at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic chokepoint through which about a fifth of global oil consumption passes annually.
Authorities confirmed there were no reported casualties or environmental impacts from either maritime incident, with the damaged tanker remaining the focus of ongoing monitoring efforts.

Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has faced heightened risks in recent weeks, with vessels reporting security incidents and shipowners adopting additional precautions as Iran and the United States stepped up hostilities.
title: UKMTO reports two tanker incidents off Oman

summary: The State Department is making its visa bond program permanent, increasing the maximum bond to $20,000, according to a draft notice published Friday in the Federal Register.

To reduce visa overstays, the Trump administration launched the program last August as part of broader efforts to curtail illegal migration. Nearly 45,500 visitors from the 50 affected countries overstayed their visas in 2024.
A nearly year-long review 'provided sufficient data' that the program enforces compliance, with pilot results showing an 83% decline in visas issued and fewer than 50 overstays recorded.
The government estimates arresting and deporting visitors who overstay visas costs about $18,000 per person, justifying the higher bond to reduce demand for B1/B2 visa applications.

Critics argue the policy imposes an 'unnecessarily harsh burden' on people from impoverished countries seeking to visit family or pursue business opportunities, while the notice becomes official on Monday.
title: US to make visa bond requirements permanent, affecting mostly African countries

The SMART-TD union praised the proposal, particularly the ban on cruise-control-like systems during certification tests. Jared Cassity, the union's top safety expert, said "Railroad certifications should represent proven ability, not simply possession of a certificate."

Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen president Wallace noted the 10-mile restriction prevents railroads from expanding operations to deeper U.S. railyards, a shift the union has resisted for years citing safety hazards from language barriers.

The Association of American Railroads declined to comment while studying the rule, and Union Pacific and CPKC did not immediately respond. This initiative mirrors Transportation Department efforts standardizing English-language communication for commercial truck drivers across border operations.
title: Trump administration pushes tougher English rules for Mexican train crews crossing into the US

summary: On Friday, President Donald Trump declared his $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund 'dead,' yet continues defending it as a standoff with two Republican senators blocks his attorney general nominee, Todd Blanche.

The fund was crafted to resolve Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS over tax records, but Senator John Cornyn and Republican Senator Thom Tillis oppose it, fearing it could compensate individuals involved in the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack.

Cornyn and Tillis are withholding support for Blanche's confirmation until the Justice Department provides written assurances terminating the fund and narrowing audit immunity for Trump and his business subsidiaries, which could extend to more than 100 entities.

During a cabinet meeting on Thursday, Trump threatened to withdraw Blanche's nomination until the senators leave office next year, urging Republicans to confirm him and warning, 'They will never get anybody like him.'

While Blanche currently serves as acting attorney general, Cornyn and Tillis hold Judiciary Committee seats expiring in January, providing leverage to stall confirmation though their long-term political influence remains limited after leaving office.

summary: On Friday, Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr defended the FCC 's early review of eight ABC local broadcast licenses, saying broadcasters have a duty to "operate in the public interest" and rejecting accusations the investigation is politically motivated.

The FCC's diversity investigation into Disney, which began last year, prompted Carr to cite the network's alleged race and gender discrimination in hiring, promotion, and compensation as raising fundamental questions about broadcast license fitness.

In its Thursday filing, ABC cited over 140,000 viewer comments posted to the FCC website, more than 95% supportive of its position, while retaining former Solicitor General Paul Clement and trial lawyer Beth Wilkinson to contest the agency's authority.

The National Association of Broadcasters warned this week that Carr's approach could affect the whole industry, stating petitions "stray well beyond" legal bounds, as ABC accused the FCC of retaliating against the network's political content.

Supreme Court Justice Neil Gorsuch recently questioned whether independent agencies might abuse power, noting businesses disfavored by the White House could face investigations, while Texas Senator Ted Cruz stated the FCC is deciding "what speech we like and what we don't" and threatening license revocation.
title: FCC chairman defends actions against ABC, says broadcasters must operate ‘in the public interest’

summary: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson defended her decision to remove Police Chief Shon Barnes as the right decision at the right time but did not explain her reasons.
The police leadership change occurred following a fatal gang-related shooting at a food festival near the Space Needle, during ongoing searches for suspects.
Both Wilson and Barnes faced criticism for delayed communication about the shootout, including information on the suspect status.

title: Seattle mayor defends ousting police chief after festival shootout

summary: Turkish national Mohammad Yousef Hasna was arrested on Friday in the United Kingdom, charged by the DOJ with conspiring to funnel money and supplies to Hamas through a purported global Sham Charity.

Prosecutors allege Hasna worked closely with senior Hamas leader Ghazi Hamad since 2023, arranging cash deliveries and smuggling materials from Egypt into the Gaza Strip while concealing warehouse locations.

The Sham Charity's gross income nearly doubled following the 2023 massacre, rising from $41.8 million in 2023 to $81.56 million in 2024, with approximately $91 million in charitable spending reported for 2025.
Hasna remains in the United Kingdom pending extradition to New York, where he faces multiple terrorism financing and material support counts, each carrying a maximum sentence of 20 years.

Counterterrorism Division Assistant Director Jarod Brown stated the investigation involved the Shin Bet and United Kingdom law enforcement, alleging the organization bypassed humanitarian safeguards to supply a "ruthless international terrorist organization.
title: Turkish man arrested in UK on US charges accusing him of aiding Hamas

summary: On a visit to Washington this week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged President Donald Trump to authorize Elon Musk to expand Starlink satellite access for guiding long-range strikes inside Russia.

Zelenskyy seeks this expanded access to improve the accuracy of longer-range systems, aiming to strike "exactly on target" rather than "in the general area," as current restrictions limit satellite use to Ukrainian territory.

Senators, including Republican Sen. Mike Rounds of South Dakota, confirmed Zelenskyy reiterated these requests during his visit, citing consistency with earlier talks at the NATO summit in Turkey two weeks ago.

During a Friday Cabinet gathering at Camp David, Trump appeared to step back from a previously discussed commitment to grant Ukraine a Patriot production license, stating "it's a hard thing to give away that kind of technology."

Intelligence reports suggest Russia is developing anti-satellite weapons to target Starlink, while Zelenskyy continues framing Ukraine's war as essential to countering Iranian-backed threats to U.S. bases in the Middle East.
title: Zelenskyy Asks Trump to Help Him Get Elon Musk's OK to Use Starlink to Help with Strikes on Russia

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the story as accountability for a “disgraced” Republican, stressing “orders,” “fined,” and “banned” to spotlight punishment and broader crackdowns on “suspicious trades,” while right-leaning coverage softens the scandal by foregrounding the settlement, the “$35,000” figure, a “three-year trading ban,” and Santos’s “denies wrongdoing” stance.

The sharpest dividing line is whether the Kalshi wager is portrayed as manipulation and misconduct or as a resolved regulatory dispute tied to a Trump-related “speech bet.” Both sides, however, agree on the core settlement and CFTC action, reflecting a shared focus on regulatory consequences amid deeper ideological differences over scandal, culpability, and political symbolism.
summary: On Friday, former Long Island Rep. George Santos agreed to pay $35,000 to resolve a Commodity Futures Trading Commission investigation into wagers he placed on the online prediction marketplace Kalshi.

The CFTC claims Santos made "material misrepresentations and omissions" about his State of the Union attendance between Feb. 12 and Feb. 25, moving contract prices to generate over $17,500 in personal profit.
Beyond the financial penalties, the settlement requires Santos to disgorge $17,569.98 in profits, pay a $17,500 civil penalty, and accept a three-year trading ban plus cease-and-desist order.
Lawyer Murray stated Friday there was "absolutely no intent to deceive any person nor attempt to manipulate any market," emphasizing the resolution involved no admission of liability.

This enforcement action signals the CFTC's intent to apply commodities law to emerging predictive markets like Kalshi, which experts like Seyhun noted involves prohibitions against "any manipulative, deceptive, or fraudulent scheme.
title: George Santos settles with CFTC over Kalshi bets

summary: On Thursday, President Donald Trump announced a "HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all armed groups in Gaza," marking a major milestone in his peace plan.

Brokered by mediators from Egypt, Qatar, Turkey, and the United States, the plan mandates a phased disarmament process with an Implementation Verification Committee overseeing weapons decommissioning and facility closure.
Israeli strikes killed at least three people in Gaza Thursday, including two children, as Gaza health officials reported the death toll has exceeded 1,200 Palestinians since the ceasefire began.
Hamas negotiator Ghazi Hamad stated the group will not act on disarmament until Israeli forces withdraw, while United States officials said Israel remains skeptical of Hamas's surrender intentions.

Cairo will soon host mediators from Egypt, Qatar, Turkey, and the United States to confirm all parties' commitment to the agreement, though officials acknowledge considerable skepticism remains on all sides.
title: Hamas Agrees to Gaza Disarmament Plan as Trump Announces Breakthrough

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the story around civilian and geopolitical fallout, emphasizing “hit by Israeli strikes,” “Iran-funded,” and even linking it to Gaza diplomacy, while right-leaning coverage turns the same event into a security victory, using charged phrases like “terror tunnels,” “boasts,” and “systematic” to portray Hezbollah as an imminent threat and Israel as decisive.

summary: On Thursday, the Israeli military destroyed a major Hezbollah tunnel system beneath the Beaufort Ridge in southern Lebanon using 700 tons of explosives, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz said in a joint statement.
Netanyahu and Katz stated the demolition occurred after Hezbollah violated the ceasefire agreement by launching a FPV drone toward an IDF engineering vehicle in southern Lebanon the previous day.

The subterranean facility, built over two decades, served as a central command center for Hezbollah's Bader Unit located about 6 kilometers from Metula. Officials described it as "a central part of the Hezbollah terror organization's invasion plan."

Residents in Metula and Misgav Am were advised to open windows due to the intensity of the explosions. The IDF has destroyed most of the tunnel system in the Beaufort area, though monitoring continues for remaining routes.

IDF forces remain on high alert, prepared for both defensive and offensive scenarios. Operations continue in the Ali Taher ridge area, where the military monitors a separate tunnel network believed to house dozens of operatives.
title: Netanyahu, Israel's Defence Minister Say Israeli Forces Destroyed Hezbollah Tunnels in Southern Lebanon
